about.title: A quieter place to talk about starting a family
body: Sri Ananth Medical Centre & Fertility Clinic was started with a simple belief: conversations about fertility and reproductive health deserve time, privacy, and a team that listens before it advises.

We know that many patients arrive here after a long and often difficult journey. Our clinic in Porur is built around that reality — calm consultation rooms, evening hours for working patients, and a team that explains every option clearly, without pressure or false promises.

Whether you're at the very first stage of wondering if something's wrong, or actively pursuing IUI or IVF elsewhere and want a second opinion, we're here to walk through it with you, one honest conversation at a time.

faqs.question: What happens at my first visit?
faqs.answer: Your first visit is mainly a conversation — we review your history, discuss any concerns, and talk through what next steps, if any, make sense. Testing is only done with your understanding of why it's being suggested.

faqs.question: How do I book an appointment?
faqs.answer: You can call or WhatsApp us directly to schedule a consultation, or use the booking option on this website.

faqs.question: Is fertility treatment covered by insurance?
faqs.answer: Coverage varies widely by insurer and policy. We recommend checking directly with your insurance provider about what fertility-related consultations and treatments are covered before your visit.

faqs.question: Will my visit be kept private?
faqs.answer: Yes. All consultations are conducted privately, and your medical information is handled in confidence, discussed only with your care team.

faqs.question: When should I consider a fertility consultation?
faqs.answer: Generally, if you've been trying to conceive for over a year (or six months if you're over 35) without success, or if you have irregular cycles or a known condition like PCOS, it's a reasonable time to talk to a specialist. If something simply feels off to you, that's reason enough to come in and ask.

blogPosts.title: When Should You See a Fertility Specialist?
blogPosts.excerpt: There's no single right moment to seek fertility care — here's a calm, honest guide to help you decide if now is the time.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Kavitha Ramaswamy
content: One of the most common questions we hear is some version of: 'Is it too early for me to come in?' The honest answer is that it's rarely too early to simply talk to someone.

As a general guideline, doctors often suggest a fertility consultation after 12 months of trying to conceive without success if you're under 35, or after 6 months if you're over 35. These are guidelines, not hard rules — they exist to help you decide when to seek support, not to make you feel like you've waited too long or come in too soon.

There are also situations where it makes sense to come in sooner: irregular or absent periods, a history of conditions like PCOS or endometriosis, previous pregnancy loss, or simply wanting to understand your reproductive health before you start trying.
A first consultation isn't a commitment to any particular treatment. It's a conversation — a chance to ask questions, understand your options, and decide what feels right for you at your own pace.

If you've been holding off on booking that first appointment, know that the goal of that visit is simply to listen and help you understand where things stand. There's no such thing as coming in with 'not enough of a reason.'
